So early stopping is a mechanism in Keras which automatically detects that after a point, if you are training the model, then there is no benefit, there is loss, there is overfitting. You can say that your loss

is increasing more or your accuracy is decreasing more. So, what does it do? It detects that state during the training and stops the training of your model at the same place. This mechanism is called early stopping. And to implement early stopping, there is a feature of callbacks in Keras. We will read callbacks in detail. There are many different types of callbacks. Callbacks is basically that you can do something after every epoch by using Keras.

early stopping and that is why you should implement early stopping. Now let's see what are the things in early stopping. So here you have some parameters. By using them, you can bring some flexibility in your early stopping mechanism. First of all, you can tell here which quantity you have to monitor, on which you want to do early stopping. So generally, you want to do it on validation loss. How much loss is coming on the new data, unseen data.

You want to measure this quantity. You can also do accuracy. If accuracy is decreasing, then early stopping will happen. If loss is increasing, then early stopping will happen. Okay. What does minimum delta tell? It is written here. Minimum change in the monitored quantity to qualify as an improvement. How much improvement you will consider, you specify that number using min delta.

After that comes patience. This is also a very important thing. Patience is the number of epochs with no improvements after which training will be stopped. Suppose there is no benefit in this epoch. So you will not stop immediately. You will wait a little more. This is called patience. You run one more epoch. And you know that there is no improvement. Then you run one more epoch. So there is still no benefit. So if you have kept patience equal to 3, then it will wait till 3 epochs.

If you have kept patience 5, then it will wait till 5 epochs. If there is no improvement, then it will do early breaking. Next is verbose. On doing verbose equal to 0, you will not be able to see this thing. Here it is written at the end. Epoch 327, early stopping. You will not be able to see this. Since I had done this, verbose equal to 1, that's why I could see this. Next is mode equal to auto. What does mode do?

Mode is one of the three. Auto, Min or Max. Now, it is written here. In Min mode, training will stop when the quantity monitored has stopped decreasing. In Max mode, it will stop when the quantity monitored has stopped increasing. It depends on the quantity that you are monitoring. If you are talking about accuracy, then it will apply something else. And if you are talking about loss, then it will apply something else.

By the way, it is best that you put auto, Keras is intelligent enough to understand what you have to do. So I always use auto. In very rare scenarios, you have to tell yourself min or max. Next is baseline. Baseline is basically baseline value for the monitored quantity. Training will stop if model doesn't show improvement over the baseline. You give a number. Next is restore. By the way, I have given none in the baseline. You can see. Restore best weights. Whether to restore model weights from the epoch with the best value of the monitored quantity.
